newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Trade Minister - WTO entry possible in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia Trade Minister - WTO entry possible in 1997.

text.p: Russian Foreign Economic Relations Minister Oleg Davydov, in talks with the European Commission, said Russia could join the World Trade Organisation in 1997, Russian media reported from Geneva on Friday.

After talks with WTO Director General Renato Ruggiero and General Council Chairman William Rossier on Thursday, Davydov said it had been decided to "speed the consideration process of Russia's (WTO) application", Kommersant Daily newspaper said.

A protocol of conditions for Russia's entry into the WTO is also being drafted, which, he said, "will contain the obligations which we will assume and the rights which we will achieve," Kommersant and RIA news agency said.
RIA also quoted him as saying the WTO working group for Russia's admission would meet on April 14, 1997 to discuss the admission protocol and a separate protocol on Russian tariffs.
Davydov said further meetings would be necessary with the U.S., European Union and "maybe two or three more countries".

Davydov also met EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan in Brussels, and the Commission urged Russia to commit itself not to introduce any new measures incompatible with World Trade Organisation (WTO) standards, a Commission official said.
